messages.author: dedca1ff91f89dec
messages.subject: MaxQtoMSstatsPTMFormat
parts:
Hello, I am trying to use MSstatsPTM for analyzing acetylome dataset (with both enriched and unenriched proteome data sets). But I have difficulty in converting the MaxQuant output to  MSstatsPTM format. 
Could you please guide me on what is format of "raw_ptm_df" in the following command, and how to generate this from MaxQ output?  
raw.input <- MaxQtoMSstatsPTMFormat(raw_ptm_df, annotation, evidence_file, proteinGroupsfile)

In addition, should I search Acetylation and proteome datasets separately or together in order to use MSstatsPTM? Thank you. 

I have been able to use MSstatsTMT sucessfully and load proteome dataset with this command: 
proteinGroups <- read.table("proteinGroups.txt", sep="\t", header=TRUE)
evidence <- read.table("evidence.txt", sep="\t", header=TRUE)
annotation.mq <- read.csv(file="MQ_Annotation.csv", header=TRUE)
input.mq <- MaxQtoMSstatsTMTFormat(evidence, proteinGroups, annotation.mq, removeProtein_with1Peptide=TRUE)

The acetylation data set MaxQ output will be similar, but with additional site file. 

Thank you. 
Xu

messages.subject: Re: MaxQtoMSstatsPTMFormat
parts:
Hi Xu,
I am having trouble reading your post because of the picture overlapping the text. I am adding an example of how to use the MaxQtoMSstatsPTM converter to the package now (which will be available on Bioc next month). For now you can checkout the development branch of the github (below). We recommend having two separate evidence files (one for Acetylation and one for proteome) but if they are in one file we can extract the unmodified peptides from the one file. Check out some of the parameters in the MaxQtoMSstatsPTM function.

https://github.com/Vitek-Lab/MSstatsPTM/blob/devel

Devon

messages.subject: Re: MaxQtoMSstatsPTMFormat
parts:
Hello,
Thank you. I now used the updated converter for my acetylome data anlaysis, and it worked well. However, there are still some issues with my data. 
I used this following lines for the format conversion for both enriched acetylome and proteome files. The generated bdt_msstatsptm_input$PTM sites is significantly less than what it should be (around half of those in maxquant generated Acetyl (K)Sites.txt).  

bdt_msstatsptm_input = MaxQtoMSstatsPTMFormat(
     evidence = evidence_ack,
     annotation = annotation_ack,
     fasta="C:/Users/cheuz/OneDrive/Desktop/BDT_Kac_analysis/BDT_Kac_sameDB_analysis20230506/test2/human_up_database.fasta",
     fasta_protein_name="uniprot_ac",
     mod_id="\\(Acetyl \\(K\\)\\)",
     evidence_prot = evidence_prot,
     proteinGroups = prot_groups,
     annotation_protein = annotation_prot,
     labeling_type = "TMT"
     ) 

Looking at the "bdt_msstatsptm_input$PTM" and compared with my original "evidence_ack", it seems any feature with multiple protein IDs in evidence_ack$Proteins and any proteins with "-" in the ID (such as Q99873-3) were not included in the results (only single protein features were used; see attached picture 1). 
I have tried to use which_proteinid_ptm = "Leading.razor.protein", however it gave an error "Error in vecseq(f__, len__, if (allow.cartesian || notjoin || !anyDuplicated(f__, :
Join results in 100241 rows; more than 91544 = nrow(x)+nrow(i). Check for duplicate key values in i each of which join to the same group in x over and over again. ..."

Another issue is that the generated PTM table have many names wthout site information (see picture 2). This could be due to the presence of non-modified proteins in enriched dataset. Should I mannually remove these features prior to input to the converter? 

Another note: I always get this information "[1] "FASTA file missing 2378 Proteins. These will be removed. This may be due to non-unique identifications.""
Don't know why this happens as I was using the exactly same fasta file for database search. This maybe due to issue with reading protein ID with "-"?
 
Any suggestions are much appreciated. Thank you very much. 

Xu
